newsitem.title: USA: Cobra Electronics buys back Kalov's stock.
newsitem.headline: Cobra Electronics buys back Kalov's stock.

text.p: Cobra Electronics Corp said Monday it has repurchased 300,000 shares of its common stock owned by president and chief executive officer Jerry Kalov, ahead of Kalov's retirement.

The shares had been part of a total of 375,000 shares purchased through the exercise of options in 1990. Under an employment agreement, Cobra lent Kalov $1.25 million for the share purchase, the company said in a news release.
Cobra paid for the purchased shares by canceling Kalov's debt to the company in the amount of about $1.9 million, which included the $1.25 million plus accrued interest.

"This transaction was made in contemplation of my retirement from Cobra at the end of this year," said Kalov. "The rest of the board felt, and I agreed, that repurchasing these shares was better for the long-term interests of the company than my selling shares on the open market," he said.

Cobra had 14 days in which to repurchase the shares at five percent below the closing price of $7.063 per share on August 7, 1997, the date that Kalov notified the company of his intention to sell these shares. In fact, Kalov, in order to create an incentive for the company to complete the transaction, agreed to sell the shares at $6.50 per share, or at a discount of about eight percent.
After the sale, Kalov will own 90,000 shares of common stock and hold options on another 491,986 shares, which are exercisable until January 3, 2000.
Shares of Cobra, which designs and markets consumer electronics products, were trading up 5/16 at 7-3/4.
